longTitle.officialTitle: To establish certain Federal agencies, effect certain reorganizations of the Federal Government, to implement certain reforms in the operation of the Federal Government and to preserve and promote the integrity of public officials and institutions, and for other purposes.

main.enactingFormula: Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representations of the United States of America in Congress assembled,

section.content: That this Act may be cited as the “Ethics in Government Act of 1978”.

main.editorialNote: [Sections 101–111, 401–405, 408, and 501–505 were repealed by section 7 of Public Law 117–286 (see additional details in footnote).]

title.heading: FINANCIAL DISCLOSURE REQUIREMENTS OF FEDERAL PERSONNEL

footnote.p: Section 7 of Public Law 117–286 provides for the repeal of sections 101–111, 401–405, 408, and 501–505 of Public Law 95–521 (Ethics in Government Act of 1978). These sections (that previously appeared in the appendix to title 5, U.S.C. prior to the enactment of such Public Law 117–286) have been restated, reorganized, and codified in various sections of chapter 131 of title 5, United States Code and should no longer be referenced as the Ethics in Government Act of 1978 (unless amending the remaining provisions of said Act).

title.editorialNote: [§112 repealed by section 3(10)(A) of P.L. 101–280, 104 Stat. 157.]
[Titles II and III were repealed by Public Law 101-194, sec. 201, approved Nov. 30, 1989, 103 Stat. 1724.]
